title: Engine-aware collation governance and dedicated runtime persistence wiring

phases.objective: Block unsupported or conflicting database collations before migration apply and route governed response chunk persistence through an independently configured runtime persistence pool.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Governed migration preflight and governed tool response chunk persistence
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Supported collation DDL passes policy, unsupported or implicit DDL is blocked, and chunk persistence fails closed without dedicated runtime persistence configuration.
steps: Detect the active database engine through the governed pool.
Evaluate migration DDL against the engine-aware charset and collation policy.
Reject unknown engines, implicit defaults, or mixed join-key collations before apply.
Resolve the dedicated runtime persistence pool for governed response chunks.
Verify least-privilege readiness and same-source chunk readback or fail closed when configuration is absent.
assertions: Unknown or undetected database engines never reach migration apply.
MariaDB/MySQL new-table DDL requires explicit utf8mb4 and policy-approved collation.
Runtime persistence uses RUNTIME_PERSISTENCE_DB_* identity rather than DB_USER fallback.
Missing dedicated runtime persistence configuration returns a bounded 503 and no durable mutation.

phases.objective: Provision and read back separate Hostinger runtime persistence identity and grants after explicit infrastructure approval.
Add runtime persistence outage recovery and collation drift reconciliation evidence.
Exercise one non-production tenant with the dedicated runtime persistence identity and governed collation readback.
Verify production grants and schema readback only after approved Hostinger provisioning and redeployment.
